newsitem.title: CANADA: Intrawest says to merge with two companies.
newsitem.headline: Intrawest says to merge with two companies.

text.p: Intrawest Corp on Wednesday said it plans to merge with Whistler Mountain Holdings Ltd. and Copper Mountain Inc of Colorado in a transaction valued at C$260 million.
Intrawest said the merger will bring the assets of the three companies together under the Intrawest name.

The Vancouver-based ski resort operator and developer also said it will seek shareholder approval to create a new class of special shares, which would distribute to the holders Intrawest's remaining equity in non-resort assets.

Intrawest said the C$260 million value of the transaction is made up of 6.1 million Intrawest common shares and the balance in cash, debt and preferred shares. The company said the 6.1 million shares will represent 20.9 percent of the company.
Executives from Whistler Mountain and Copper Mountain will also join Intrawest's board of directors.

Intrawest also announced it will make a capital investment of more than C$35 million for Whistler Mountain enhancements and will complete the village plan for Whistler's Creekside. Intrawest said Copper Mountain will receive more than C$35 million in capital improvements, including new lifts.

"The combination of these three companies and their assets now position Intrawest to emerge as the leader in the ongoing consolidation of the North American ski resort industry," said Joe Houssian, president and chief executive of Intrawest, in a statements.

The three companies together had a combined 4.5 million skier visits in 1995/1996, compared with 2.8 million for Intrawest alone, the company said. Intrawest said it now has a roster of eight ski resorts in two countries.
Intrawest said the transactions are subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals and are expected to close in March, 1997.
